key_idea: A firework only covers downwards, so the deepest uncovered node forces a firework on its ancestor path and the highest allowed ancestor (k-1 up, or the root) dominates every other choice.
sketch: Process nodes in decreasing index (valid bottom-up order since p_i<i), maintaining need[v] = largest distance from v to a still-uncovered node in its subtree. When need[v]==k-1, or v is the root with something uncovered, place a firework at v and reset need to -1; otherwise push need[v]+1 to the parent. O(n). Exchange argument gives optimality. Pitfalls: k=1 means every node needs its own firework; the root must always be handled; depth can be 1e5 so avoid recursion. Any optimal set is accepted, so sample 1 differs textually (I print {1,2} instead of {1,5}); samples_passed is true because my own validator plus an exhaustive subset brute force confirmed validity and minimality on 1500 random trees with n<=9.
